turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Right, obs are done. Blood pressure's one eighteen over seventy four, pulse 72, and oxygen sats 98 percent. Head on in.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): G'day. Come and sit yourself down. What's brought you in?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Um, I rolled my ankle. Yesterday, at footy.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ah, that's no good. Tell me how it went, in your own words.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. I stepped to change direction and it just went over, on the outside.
[SEG0006] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I was on the sideline at training last night, round seven. He limped off but he stayed till the end.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Since then, how's it feeling? The swelling, the walking, all of that.
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): It's been swollen since yesterday, the right one. I can walk on it but it hurts. I don't know how bad, it's just sore.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Show me where the sore bit is.
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): Round the outside. Uh, the right ankle, not really up in the toes.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any numbness, or pins and needles in that foot?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Uh, I don't think so.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Has this ankle given you trouble before today, or is it all new?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): It's been a bit niggly since last winter, or the one before. I don't know, doctor. I can't date it.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's ok, we don't need the exact week. Have you taken anything for the pain?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): Umm neurofen, three hundred, err, two hundred milligrams, twice a day since last night. And two panadol this morning, the five hundred ones.
[SEG0017] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I iced it when we got home and stuck his foot up on a cushion. He was pretty grumpy about missing the cooldown.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fair enough. Any illnesses that run in the family, while I've got you?

[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Umm my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, my other sister has pressure but no sugar, and my nan's got arthritis in her knees. My brother doesn't have any of that.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): And what's ordinary life like? Work, the hours, what you eat, training, a drink, the lot.

[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): I work at the sports shop in town, err about twenty five hours a week, mostly arvos and Saturdays. Diet's plain, meat and veg, bit of takeaway after training. I train three nights a week with the under nineteens, and I have two beers on a Saturday, nothing through the week.
[SEG0022] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Traffic was a shocker getting over here, mind you. Bridge was stopped dead for ages.
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah we just sat there. Some bloke had a flat, I think. Nothing moving.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ha, that bridge at this hour is always a gamble. Catch any of the cricket last night?
[SEG0025] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Yeah the Aussies were going alright till the rain. Typical, sun one minute and then it's bucketing down.
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): I only saw the highlights. That catch at midwicket was a good one.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Righto, back to this ankle. I'll have a feel, so sing out if it's too much.
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Ok. Uh, go easy, I don't know.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's swelling over the outside of the right ankle, and it's tender in the ligament just in front of the bone, not on the bone itself. Medial side's quiet.
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Ow. Yeah. That's the spot. Sorry.

[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ottawa rules, I'll say them out loud. We x-ray if there's bony tenderness along the back of the lateral malleolus or the medial malleolus, or if you can't take four steps. Can you walk four steps for me?
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah. Hurts, but I can. One, two, three, four.
[SEG0033] person_1 (NURSE): Mm. He's getting the weight through, just a bit ginger on the right.

[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ta. You manage four steps and I can't find bony tenderness, so I'd call this a lateral ligament sprain for now, not a break. I won't get an x-ray unless it worsens. Rest it, keep it elevated when you sit, and ice it about twenty minutes at a time, no footy till it's settled.
[SEG0035] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He's got a game Saturday week. What if he's still limping?

[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): If it's not better in ten days, or the swelling blows up, or he can't put weight on it, come straight back and we'll x-ray it then. You're welcome to check in sooner if you're worried.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): Ok. I don't know, doctor, I just hope it chills out. Thanks.

spec.situation: Young player who twisted the ankle yesterday; swelling, can bear weight with pain; doctor applies Ottawa rules aloud, no X-ray unless it worsens; rest and elevation advice.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

bad.reason: Swelling since yesterday is supported; lateral location is only doctor-observed, not patient-reported.
bad.text: Ankle swelling (category=musculoskeletal, status=present, duration=1 day, onset=yesterday, temporality=current, body_site=lateral right ankle, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Mechanism of injury was inversion-type: he stepped to change direction and the right ankle 'went over, on the outside' at football training yesterday.
Walking is possible but painful / limping: patient said he can walk on it but it hurts, caregiver said he limped off, and nurse noted weight-bearing was ginger on the right.
Panadol dose is recorded incorrectly/incompletely: patient took two 500 mg tablets this morning (total 1 g), not '500 mg' alone.
Family history negatives stated: mother did not have diabetes, brother does not have diabetes/high blood pressure/arthritis, and father's diabetes began in his fifties.
Examination detail missing: tenderness was in the ligament just in front of the lateral malleolus, not on the bone itself.
Doctor explicitly said no X-ray now and would not get one unless it worsens.
Return precautions were more specific: come straight back if not better in 10 days, if swelling 'blows up', or if he cannot put weight on it; can return sooner if worried.
